title: The Orion Nebula
caption: The Orion Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, La Silla, Chile
celestial: M 42, Messier 42, Orion Nebula · constellation Orion · about 1400 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This image of the Orion Nebula, also known as Messier 42, was made using the Wide Field Imager, a camera mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, which stands at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. It is a composite of several exposures taken through five different filters.

The Orion Nebula is a star-forming region, a cloud of gas in which new stars are being born. It is classed as an emission nebula, or H II region: hydrogen gas that glows because hot young stars are flooding it with energetic light. That glowing hydrogen is one of the things this image was designed to capture.

Each filter admits a different slice of light. Combining them into one picture lets astronomers show several kinds of emission at once, from the ultraviolet end of the spectrum to the red glow of hydrogen, so that different parts of the cloud and its stars stand out from one another.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (35.49 x 34.10 arcminutes) and distance (1400 light years), the frame spans roughly 14 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 1,400 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope. Red-filter light and glowing hydrogen are shown in red, yellow-green light in green, blue light in blue and ultraviolet light in purple.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet light shown in purple is invisible to the eye, and exposures of nearly an hour per filter gather far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

alt: The Orion Nebula, a large glowing cloud of gas.
